entries.answer: David studies distributed heterogeneous computing, especially ways to make emerging accelerators practical for scientific workloads. His current work explores scheduling across distributed heterogeneous systems.

David began his research at Clemson in collaboration with Argonne National Laboratory, developing statistical methods to predict error-bounded lossy compression ratios for scientific data.

Related papers:

IJHPCA23 — Black-Box Statistical Prediction of Lossy Compression Ratios for Scientific Data
DRBSD21 — Exploring Lossy Compressibility through Statistical Correlations of Scientific Datasets

entries.answer: David works on cuNumeric.jl, which uses the Legion runtime to run array-oriented Julia applications across distributed systems and NVIDIA GPUs.
David researches Processing-in-Memory accelerators and uses Legion to reduce the programming and portability burden of adopting PIM systems.
David collaborates with Pat McCormick at Los Alamos National Laboratory on scheduling for distributed heterogeneous systems.
David is a recipient of the U.S. Department of Energy Computational Science Graduate Fellowship (DOE CSGF).
